body:
WHAT
The packaging step bundles the engine host (engine/host/dist/main.js) and all its dependencies into one minified CommonJS file, build-resources/engine/engine.cjs, with esbuild. The packaged app spawns it with Electron's own Node (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1). No node_modules directory is shipped.

WHY
Shipping node_modules makes the package huge and fragile; a single file has nothing to resolve at runtime.

WHERE
app/scripts/bundle-engine.js — ENTRY, OUT_FILE (engine.cjs), the esbuild.build({ bundle: true, platform: "node", format: "cjs", minify: true, alias: { "@vscode/ripgrep": RIPGREP_SHIM } }) call, plus DOC_EXTRACT_OUT (doc-extract.mjs) and TUI_OUT (tui.mjs); the 'Engine not built' guard. app/package.json — build.files lists only package.json and build-resources/app; extraResources copies engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs and rg. app/main.js — engineEntryPoint() uses process.resourcesPath/engine/engine.cjs with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE when app.isPackaged.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. After bundle-engine.js runs, build-resources/engine/engine.cjs exists, is a single file, and contains no `require("@magentra/` or `require("zod")`-style unresolved bare specifiers except Node built-ins.
2. Running `node build-resources/engine/engine.cjs --help` (or --serve with a bad cwd) from a directory with no node_modules starts without 'Cannot find module'.
3. bundle-engine.js exits nonzero with 'Engine not built' when engine/host/dist/main.js is missing.
4. package.json build.files does not include node_modules and extraResources filter is exactly engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs and rg/rg.exe.
5. In a packaged run engineEntryPoint() returns command process.execPath, args [<resources>/engine/engine.cjs], env { ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1' }.
